correctness.rationale: Unitality gives the bijection B(x,y)=λ(xy) exactly, including nonsymmetric bilinear forms. In vertex-arrow basis its Gram matrix is [D U;V 0], where column a of U and row a of V are supported on source and target of active arrow a. Kernel equations Vx=0 force target coordinates zero; Dx modulo im U imposes uncovered nonzero diagonal constraints. This yields rank |S_F|+|T_F|+#{v outside S_F∪T_F:d_v≠0}, independent of active arrow coefficient values. Counting support weights and uncovered diagonals gives the polynomial; all arrow activation yields max n+|S_all∩T_all|. Equality m=|S_all∩T_all| forces every nonisolated vertex indegree=outdegree=1 (directed cycles). Fresh small-quiver exact GF2 direct ranks confirm chain/fork distinction; the algebraic proof covers arbitrary q, loops, and parallel arrows.
